_comment: 🧩️ TSV IANA/✳️any's own contribution to the repository test platform — its mutation oracle registration and its declared mutation vocabulary (wave 7, ticket 26/08/23/END-TO-END-TESTING-REFACTOR). Discovered by convention alongside ✏️s/🔌️plugins/🗄️stdio's own top-level manifest; merged into one registry, no central edit required. Reuses the already-linked `csv` crate (the shared stdio manifest's `csv` entry covers RFC 4180 creation only, capability `tabular-csv`; this subset registers its own id for `tsv-iana-mutate` instead of reusing that entry, which would fail the contract's oracle-capability-mismatch check), reconfigured for IANA TSV: tab delimiter, no quoting at all (`QuoteStyle::Never` on write, `quoting(false)` on read) — TSV has no escaping mechanism, unlike RFC 4180 CSV.

oracles.rationale: The same reference reader/writer of the Rust ecosystem the shared `csv` entry already uses for RFC 4180, reconfigured here for IANA text/tab-separated-values: tab delimiter, quoting disabled entirely on both read and write. IANA TSV (https://www.iana.org/assignments/media-types/text/tab-separated-values) draws no header/data distinction and has no quoting/escaping mechanism, so a field can never legally carry a literal tab or newline byte; this subset's real fixture was checked for both at derivation time and carries neither. Drives every declared `TsvMutation` kind independently of this repository's own byte-exact split/rejoin codec, including the two real serialization concerns this subset's vocabulary makes substantive: `set-trailing-newline` and `set-line-ending` genuinely add/remove/rewrite bytes, so `semantic-tabular-mutate-v1` keeps both fields live in the comparison instead of ignoring them the way the base `semantic-tabular-v1` profile does for RFC 4180's writer-freedom equivalents.

comparisonProfiles.description: TSV tables compared by the full record grid PLUS the trailing-newline and line-ending choices as normative fields. Differs from the base `semantic-tabular-v1` profile only in that `trailingNewline` and `lineTerminator` are NOT ignored: this subset's vocabulary declares `set-trailing-newline` and `set-line-ending` as real mutation kinds that genuinely rewrite bytes (IANA TSV has no header/data distinction to make substantive the way RFC 4180's `has_header` convention does, so its own real serialization concerns fill that role instead), and they have to actually participate in the comparison or those scenarios are no-ops.
